_template: Canonical harness.json. /harness-init copies this to .harness/harness.json and dev-ops fills every test_kinds.cmd by RUNNING it. See templates/README.md.
_test_matrix_note: change_type -> required test kinds. A FLOOR, not a ceiling: qa may add kinds it infers from the diff, never drop below. Predicate names in `when` are FIXED DATA so the gate is auditable; qa evaluates them against the diff.
_test_kinds_note: EVERY cmd ships as null. dev-ops replaces it with a command it has RUN and seen pass, or leaves it null and REPLACES the placeholder _reason with the real one. NEVER write a plausible-looking command you have not executed: `node --test src/` reports `tests 1 / fail 1` for a module-load error, which reads exactly like a failing suite (DEC-98). A null cmd is a not-applicable soft skip in the qa gate; an invented cmd turns a hard gate into a silent no-op, which is strictly worse. DELETE the _reason on any kind whose cmd you fill — leaving 'unset, detection has not run' beside a verified command is a lie about the project's own config. `exclude` keeps worktree and vendor dirs out of diff scans — measured 3x test-file inflation in kaya-ai without it.

unit._reason: unset — dev-ops has not run detection yet

component._reason: unset — dev-ops has not run detection yet

ui._reason: unset — dev-ops has not run detection yet. If the project has no browser-driver, leave null: qa records `ui: skipped (no browser target)` and does NOT fail.

eval._reason: unset — dev-ops has not run detection yet. Required only for change_type: ai_behavior; ai-dev authors the eval, qa gates it.

typecheck._reason: unset — dev-ops has not run detection yet. Not in the matrix; available for qa to add.

_commit_attribution_note: Recovery derives what landed from `git log` rather than trusting a state file, and review scope depends on telling human edits from agent commits (SPEC 15.3).
_dirty_tree_note: A dirty tree halts a team with BLOCKED. Without this whitelist the harness's own run artifacts would deadlock the next run.
_cost_model_note: Rates in USD per million tokens, VERIFIED 2026-07-26 against platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing.md. The four token classes are priced SEPARATELY and must never be summed into one 'input' number: a cache read is 0.1x base input, a 5m cache write 1.25x, a 1h cache write 2x. Cache reads are typically the largest token class by volume and the smallest by cost — pricing them at base input rate overstates a run by ~10x on its biggest line. Every model is a LIST of dated rate periods so a price change cannot silently mis-report; cost-report.py picks the period covering the run date and REFUSES to price a model whose periods do not cover it.

claude-sonnet-5._note: Standard pricing. A config that hardcoded only the intro rate would under-report Sonnet 5 spend by 50% from this date.

cost_model._modifier_note: The transcript records three price-affecting fields per message — `speed`, `inference_geo`, `service_tier` — and IGNORING THEM IS A SILENT HALVING. Fast mode on Opus 5 bills $10/$50 instead of $5/$25, and it is one `/fast` away in any session; a cost report that assumes standard speed would report half the true spend with no indication anything was wrong. cost-report.py groups tokens by (model, speed, inference_geo) and REFUSES to price a combination it has no entry for.

fast._note: Not a multiplier — fast mode has its OWN published rates, and only on Opus 5 / Opus 4.8. Caching multipliers still apply on top of them.

inference_geo._note: US-only inference applies 1.1x to every token class on Claude 4.6+. `global` and `not_available` are standard.

cost_model._server_tool_note: Charged on top of tokens. Web fetch and code execution alongside web search are free; standalone code execution bills per container-hour after a large monthly free tier, which a single-operator harness will not reach.

_budgets_note: Cost is the post-build signal (DEC-99), so it needs a bound as well as a meter. These sit alongside max_cycles in the team config: max_cycles bounds RETRIES, these bound SPEND. A team that exceeds its budget stops and escalates rather than continuing — the same BLOCKED path an exhausted cycle budget takes. Measured anchor: one dev-ops detection spawn on claude-fable-5 cost $2.72 (DEC-114), so these are single-digit numbers of spawns, not hundreds.

budgets._per_feature_rationale: SC-1 kills the org above $50/feature. The budget IS the criterion, not a separate guess.
